**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good
- Narrow, well-placed fix: `align_from_axes` returns the held alignment untouched when the turn is negligible, so `change_of` sees no change and the existing refusal fires; GUI Apply check and MCP `set_part_axes` share that path.
- Threshold (`axis.rs` `is_no_turn`): vector part of the unit quaternion is sin(angle/2), bound `LAND_TOL/8` = 1.25e-10, so angle <= 2.5e-10 rad (under 0.25 nm at 1 m). That is a quarter of the 1e-9 the landing proof already accepts as "on the axis", so no re-orientation a user could tell apart is swallowed. It is far tighter than `is_identity_rot` (about 2.8e-6 rad), which the decision file rightly rejects.
- A 180 degree flip has vector part norm 1 and is a turn; a swapped pick pair or flipped pick changes the frame, so it is a real turn too. The test is on the vector part, so q and -q both read as no turn, correctly.
- Order of refusals is kept: degenerate/NaN picks fail in `dir_through`, the crossing check, `quat_from_axes` (non-finite) before `is_no_turn`; a NaN rotation would compare false (read as a turn) anyway. The landing proof and finite check still run on the returned alignment.
- Undo: the refusal is raised at command creation, nothing is stored; both tests assert history/state unchanged.
- Decision file, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1347` present. No unwrap/expect/panic added outside tests (only in test code). No process files touched.

## Results
On the self-hosted runner, merged with main 0fa183de: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43472518260 - success. Quick gate: app suites ok (76 s, 0 failed); clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` clean. Not run locally (no Windows-only reading in the diff).

## Tests, by reasoning (old code not run)
- `re_applying_the_same_two_axis_picks_refuses_as_already_held`: old code re-composed an identity turn with float noise (y -7.499999999999999 vs -7.5), so `change_of` found a change and the second call returned Ok; `expect_err` fails on old code. Pins GUI `check_align` too.
- `set_part_axes_again_with_the_same_picks_refuses_as_already_held`: same mechanism through MCP; `c.refused` fails on old code. Also checks no extra undo step.
- `a_real_further_turn_from_the_held_alignment_still_goes_through`: a guard test; it would pass on old code too, by design. It does show a 180 degree-class real turn is not swallowed and undo restores exactly.

## Notes (not blocking)
- With no stored alignment and picks already aligned with the world, `held` is the default identity; whether that refuses or stores depends on `change_of`'s handling of "none vs identity" - not tested here, harmless either way.
- No unit test places a turn just above/below 2.5e-10 rad; the reasoning above is sound but not pinned.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
